hero.heading: Where does discipline cost you time and let complexity compound?
hero.subtitle: I guide your organisation to eliminate discipline-based tasks, so only the discipline that is truly necessary remains. Together we reduce the work to its essentials. Then we embed the decisions already made into your system landscape, until deviating from them becomes impossible.
hero.fit: For organisations whose system landscape grew faster than it was designed.
whycurfee.heading.1: Complexity is not a discipline problem.
whycurfee.body.1: Most organisations don't suffer from a lack of discipline. The complexity of their system landscapes compounds because these grew faster than they were designed: one pragmatic decision at a time, without anyone maintaining the overall perspective.
whycurfee.body.2: I want organisations to invest their time and money in work that creates value for their business and employees. That's why I founded Curfee. I don't start with recommendations or ready-made frameworks. I start:
whycurfee.start.1: With your system landscape that has grown organically.
whycurfee.start.2: With workflows that function because someone quietly maintains them.
whycurfee.start.3: With the decisions that have been made but never embedded.
whycurfee.payoff: That is the core of my work: making reality visible, reducing it to its essentials, and embedding decisions until simplicity becomes self-sustaining.
howiwork.1.title: Root cause over symptoms.
howiwork.1.body: Symptoms reveal the direction. Root causes demand resolution. The work begins where the chain ends.
howiwork.2.title: Structure over discipline.
howiwork.2.body: A standard that depends on individual discipline is not sustainable. Each embedded decision becomes a compounding improvement, and the work done once stays done.
howiwork.3.title: Solid foundation over workaround.
howiwork.3.body: Workarounds lead to a structure that no one chose. Lay a solid foundation, and you can build anything upon it.
whycurfee.conclusion: The structure carries what discipline used to carry.
whycurfee.conclusion.label: Decisions that enforce themselves
hero.visual.aria: Diagram: recurring, discipline-based tasks, reduced to the essentials and embedded as decisions that the structure enforces
observations.heading.status_quo: Does any of this sound familiar?
observations.1.title: Discipline Dependency
observations.1.reality: Conventions survive only as long as someone is watching.
observations.2.title: Structural Fragility
observations.2.reality: Dependencies have grown beyond what anyone fully understands.
observations.3.title: Decisions Without Effect
observations.3.reality: Decisions were documented on paper or in wikis, but nowhere were they consistently enforced.
observations.4.title: Knowledge Concentration
observations.4.reality: Knowledge lives in people's heads and disappears when they leave.
observations.5.title: Workarounds as the Norm
observations.5.reality: What started as an exception is now a new norm.
observations.7.title: AI-Assisted Collaboration
observations.7.reality: AI-generated content reaches the organisation landscape faster than the current structure can integrate it.
schema.service.description: Curfee offers structural architecture across systems, software, and workflows, delivered as high-value, project-based engagements rather than hourly services. Each engagement starts from the current reality of a system landscape, uncovers the root causes behind recurring struggles, and embeds decisions in pipelines and tooling so the system itself enforces them, independent of individual discipline. Available across Austria, Germany, and Switzerland (DACH region).
about.heading: I am Philipp Höllinger.
about.background.heading: Where my approach comes from
about.credentials.1.title: Roots in Logistics
about.credentials.1.body: I started by coordinating workflows between goods, employees, and processes.
about.credentials.1.lesson: When people with different approaches work together, structure matters more than discipline.
about.credentials.2.title: From Computer Science to Architecture
about.credentials.2.body: After computer science, I moved into software engineering and then to architecture.
about.credentials.2.lesson: Keep the big picture and the details in sight; for me, one is incomplete without the other.
about.credentials.3.title: Addition by Subtraction
about.credentials.3.body: Most system landscapes I encountered suffered from bloat: too many tools, discipline-based standards, and inflated workflows.
about.credentials.3.lesson: Improvements usually come from reduction, and that's precisely where the real gain lies.
about.credentials.4.title: Decision Enforcement
about.credentials.4.body: I kept watching well-documented decisions get ignored in practice. People remember a convention until their focus moves elsewhere.
about.credentials.4.lesson: When the structure enforces a decision, the agreed way becomes the only way, and errors approach zero.
about.credentials.5.title: Continuous Improvement
about.credentials.5.body: Every project taught me the same asymmetry: an embedded decision keeps paying off, a shortcut keeps costing until someone deals with it.
about.credentials.5.lesson: When structure comes first, improvements compound instead of complexity.
about.credentials.6.title: Structure in the Age of AI
about.credentials.6.body: Everything the path taught me counts double in the age of AI. An AI does not get tired and does not forget the agreed way of working. It does not remember it either: whatever is not built into the system stays invisible to it.
about.credentials.6.lesson: AI produces exactly what the system allows.
manifest.text: Doing less is harder than doing more.
engagements.heading: Selected engagements
engagements.1.title: Double-booking a courtroom became impossible.
engagements.1.body: A court booking system enabled the very errors it was meant to prevent: double-booked courtrooms, past-dated bookings, unchecked conflicts. I guided the rebuild and designed integrity into every layer, from validation rules to database constraints. A booking that conflicts with another can no longer be saved.
engagements.1.diagram.aria: Diagram: a courtroom calendar where a second hearing in an occupied slot is refused and a hearing in a free slot is booked
engagements.2.title: A summer job became a single click.
engagements.2.body: For years, five students spent each summer reading organiser emails and typing every event into the system by hand. I designed the flow around self-service: organisers submit their own listings and an automated import loads them daily. All that remains is to check the content, adjust a detail where needed, and click publish. Nobody types an event into the system any more.
engagements.2.diagram.aria: Diagram: organisers fill a self-service event form, entries import daily, one click publishes them
engagements.2.diagram.form.title: Submit your event
engagements.3.title: Every publication became bilingual.
engagements.3.body: The EU Single Digital Gateway required administrative information to be structured, multilingual, and machine-readable, yet no system could produce it. I designed the publishing system around predefined fields and an enforced translation step: editors fill the fields in German, and nothing goes live until the English translation exists. Metadata and publication run on their own.
engagements.3.diagram.aria: Diagram: editors fill predefined fields in German, a page can only go public once the English translation exists
engagements.3.diagram.form.title: Predefined fields
about.who.hero.1: I'm not interested in the next big hype. My goal is to reduce complexity through structures built on forward-looking decisions: once embedded, they enforce themselves and prepare the organisation for what comes next.
about.who.quote: What drives me is an obsession with the things that go unnoticed, the small details that shape the future of an environment.
about.who.why.3: Before I change anything, I want to understand how it affects an organisation and the people working with it. The most common mistake I have seen is the opposite: systems, software, and workflows implemented first and understood later.
about.who.why.2: I am a minimalist and call myself an advocate of simple concepts. They outlast any sophisticated process that runs on discipline and quietly breaks over time. And small changes that keep paying off over time create as much value as one big fix for one big pain.

privacy.personal.heading: Processing of personal data
privacy.personal: Personal data is collected only to the extent technically necessary, with purpose limitation and data minimisation applied throughout. Collected data is never disclosed to third parties without a legal basis. Three legal grounds may apply. Consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) covers cases where you have given consent for one or more specific purposes. Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) covers cases where processing is needed to perform a contract you are party to, or to take steps at your request before entering into one. Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) covers cases where processing is necessary for legitimate interests of the controller or a third party, unless those interests are overridden by your fundamental rights and freedoms.
privacy.rights.heading: Rights of data subjects
privacy.rights: As a data subject, you have the following rights. Access (Art. 15 GDPR): confirmation whether your personal data is being processed, along with information about such data and its processing. Rectification (Art. 16 GDPR): correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data. Erasure (Art. 17 GDPR): deletion of your personal data, subject to the conditions laid down in Art. 17. Restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR): limits on how your personal data is processed. Data portability (Art. 20 GDPR): a copy of your personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format. Objection (Art. 21 GDPR): the right to object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to processing of your personal data.
privacy.withdrawal.heading: Right to withdraw consent
privacy.withdrawal: Pursuant to Art. 7(3) GDPR, you have the right to withdraw consent at any time. The lawfulness of processing carried out on the basis of consent before its withdrawal is not affected. Withdrawal can be declared by email.
privacy.complaint.heading: Right to lodge a complaint
privacy.complaint: If you believe that the processing of your personal data violates the GDPR, you have the right, pursuant to Art. 77 GDPR, to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority.
privacy.ssl.heading: SSL/TLS encryption
privacy.ssl: For security reasons and to protect the transmission of personal data, this website uses SSL or TLS encryption. You can identify an encrypted connection by the fact that the browser's address bar starts with 'https://'.
privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies and stored data
privacy.cookies: This website sets no cookies and stores nothing about its visitors. Tracking, profiling, and third-party scripts that would set cookies or persist information on your device are absent. The only data processed is what is technically required to deliver the page (see the Hosting section below). One exception: if you switch the language via the toggle in the footer, your choice is stored locally in your browser (localStorage) so the site opens in your language on the next visit. This information never leaves your device.

privacy.links: This website contains links to third-party websites. When you follow such external links, data may be transmitted to the respective operator. The controller accepts no liability for the content and data processing by third parties. Users are encouraged to review the privacy policies of linked websites.
privacy.hosting.heading: Hosting
privacy.hosting: This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, provided by GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P Kelly Jr St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. Accessing the site automatically records information in server log files: IP address, date and time of access, requested resources, and the browser and operating system used. schema.decision.enforcement.name: Decision Enforcement Principle
schema.decision.enforcement.description: The Decision Enforcement Principle is an architecture approach in which decisions are enforced by the system itself, through pipelines, automated checks, and tool configuration, regardless of individual discipline, memory, or vigilance. Developed and applied by Philipp Höllinger at Curfee across systems, software, and workflows, the principle treats a decision as embedded only when the structure carries it forward without human intervention. It is the core principle behind every Curfee engagement.
